The political scale is at least two dimensional, whereas most people think of it in one dimension, a line from Left to Right. More accurately, there is a Left, a Right, an Up, and a Down. The core meaning of Left is "anti-property rights". The core meaning of Right is "pro-property rights". Then after you've calibrated that axis, you must now calibrate the other one. The core meaning of Up is "Collectivism", and the core meaning of Down is "Individualism".

If you are both "anti-property rights" and "collectivist", then you'd a Communist. If you are both "anti-property rights" and "individualist", then you'd be an Anarchist.

If you are both "pro-property rights" and "collectivist", then you'd be a Fascist. If you are both "pro-property rights" and "individualist", then you'd be a Libertarian.

National Socialism doesn't fit into any of those four groupings, because they all assume total adherence to both axes on the graph. But while National Socialism is heavily Collectivist on the up/down axis, he clearly wanted room on the individual side as well. When it comes to the left/right axis, Hitler was a centrist. He saw the good parts of both anti-property rights and pro-property rights outlooks, and strived to balance them. He explained that in this quote:

"I define from the word 'social' meaning in the main 'social equity'. A Socialist is one who serves the common good without giving up his individuality. Our adopted term 'Socialist' has nothing to do with Marxist Socialism. Marxism is anti-property; true socialism is not. Marxism places no value on the individual or individual effort, of efficiency, true socialism values the individual and encourages him in individual efficiency, at the same time holding that his interests as an individual must be in consonance with the community."

Hitler valued both individualism and collectivism, he valued both the right to private property and the fruits of your labor, but only up to a point, and after that point you were expected to also be able to see the anti-property rights argument, as well. His whole system was about creating societal balance.

It's very clear that Hitler was an Authoritarian Centrist. I'm not sure how it happened, but for some reason we call that far Right now. I think that's because many people aren't aware that the Collectivism/Individualism scale and the Left/Right scale are in no way connected.
